uploads/science/Scipad/Year 9 Book 1/Wor.searchText: BOTANY - PLANT SCIENCE Pollination Animals, birds, fish and insects look for mates in order to reproduce. Since plants can’t walk, swim or fly, most of them need help moving the pollen from one flower to another. Some plants are pollinated by the wind, but many of them produce flowers to attract pollinators. uploads/science/Scipad/Year 9 Book 1/Wor.searchText: BOTANY - PLANT SCIENCE Fertilisation Pollination is the transfer of pollen from one plant to another, whereas fertilisation is the fusion of male and female gametes. Pollen contains the male gametes (sperm) and the ovary, at the base of the stigma, contains the female gamete (egg cell). uploads/science/Scipad/Year 9 Book 1/Wor.searchText: BOTANY - PLANT SCIENCE Seed Structure The cotyledon (pronouced “cot-il-lee-don”) is an embryonic leaf within a seed. They are not true leaves but will photosynthesise for a short time to supply energy so the true leaves can grow. uploads/science/Scipad/Year 9 Book 1/Wor.searchText: BOTANY - PLANT SCIENCE Seed Dispersal A seed contains a new plant and a store of food. Plants produce large numbers of seeds because only a few grow successfully into mature plants. In the wild, most seeds never even get to germinate (start growing). Seed dispersal involves the spreading of seeds over a distance. They need to be dispersed away from the parent plant, or they will suffer from competition for light and space as well as for nutrients
